source_statement: For a self-dual Artin representation rho of G_Q whose conductor is coprime to N_E, w(E,rho)=w(E)^(dim rho) sign(alpha_rho) (alpha_rho/N_E), where alpha describes det rho and the dyadic symbol is explicitly normalized by alpha modulo8.

actual_applications.argument: Use rho=chi_k0 on E^h. The fixed actual k0 is negative odd fundamental, prime to N_(E^h). Its local-square requirements at every prime of2Nh imply chi_k0(N_(E^h))=1: E^h has good reduction away from2Nh, so its conductor has no other support. Since chi_k0(-1)=-1 and w(E^h)=-1 from the prepared odd-sign filter, the twist has root number+1. This does not choose k0, prove the filter or assert uniform analytic constants.

actual_applications.argument: Use rho=chi_hstar on E. The actual hstar is negative odd fundamental and a square at primes of2N, as specified3279–3285 and14830–14842. Thus its conductor is coprime to N and the theorem gives exactly w(E^hstar)=w(E)chi_hstar(-N). The independent identity w(E)=-product w_(p^e) and the nonzero-central-value sign are not supplied by this source.
